The *Lakkhaṇahārasampāta* ("Conveying Characteristics: Combined Treatment", Ne 24) is a section of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, an exegetical treatise belonging to the late canonical or paracanonical Pali literature [SuttaCentral]. In the methodology of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, the text constitutes a combined treatment (*sampāta*) examining how characteristic marks (*lakkhaṇa*) are systematically applied to doctrinal exposition [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language and lists no external parallels [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 87 matching passages across 10 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the canonical suttas, it shares notable passages with the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), consisting of 14 matches (including segment §2.5_0–2.5_2 matching AN §105.2.2_0–105.2.2_3) [DharmaNexus]. The section is closely integrated with other *sampāta* chapters of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, sharing material with the *Samāropanahārasampāta* (Ne 35), *Otaraṇahārasampāta* (Ne 31), *Yuttihārasampāta* (Ne 22), and *Vevacanahārasampāta* (Ne 29) [DharmaNexus]. In commentarial and subcommentarial literature, the text is heavily cited and analyzed in the subcommentary *Nettivibhāvinī* (29 matches) and the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (27 matches), with additional reuse matches occurring in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Aṅguttaranikāye Ekakanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language alignments meeting the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
